title: This water is faster than an Olympic swimmer 🌊
subject: ocean
description:
Would you know which way to swim? 👇

Rip currents are narrow channels of water moving away from the beach at up to 8 feet per second, faster than an Olympic swimmer. They don't pull you under. People drown because they panic and swim straight back against the current until they're exhausted. About 100 people die in them in the U.S. every year, and lifeguards rescue around 30,000 more.

Sources: NOAA National Ocean Service, "What is a rip current?"; NOAA SciJinks, "Rip Currents"; National Weather Service / United States Lifesaving Association, rip current safety brochure; Smithsonian Ocean, "Rip Current Science".

scenes.text: You're swimming hard, and the beach keeps getting farther away.
That's a rip current, a narrow channel racing out to sea at up to 8 feet per second.
NOAA says that's faster than an Olympic swimmer.
It doesn't pull you under. People drown swimming straight back against it until their arms give out.
About 100 Americans die in them every year, and they cause over 80 percent of surf lifeguard rescues.
The way out: swim parallel to the beach, then angle back to shore.
